metadata.title: Build a Futurama-Style Toy Enterprise in Blender, from Images
metadata.render_by: Professor Bear, with his own tools (film source only)

beats.narration_text: This is Liam. This is a toy Enterprise in a Futurama style, as Grok Bot finished it in Blender. This film isn't the story of how it was made. It's one way you could build something like it, from these pictures and a coding agent.
beats.on_screen: Brutalist opening over the hero render

beats.narration_text: Read the images first. The side view gives you the saucer's thickness, the neck and the secondary hull. The top view gives you the round saucer and the nacelle spacing. The front view shows the width and the deflector. Notice it's built from simple round shapes.
beats.on_screen: Side, top, front renders with axes outside the ship
beats.label: axes, major volumes

beats.narration_text: Pick a working scale. Call the saucer ten units across and measure everything else against it in the side and top views. And decide which design you are matching. Here it's the toy concept, with the blueprints as a proportion check, not both at once.
beats.on_screen: Concept image beside the hero render
beats.label: target design

beats.narration_text: Checkpoint one: block out the four big forms. A flattened sphere for the saucer, a capsule for the secondary hull, two cylinders for the nacelles, and a box for the neck. Nothing else. Then compare side and top views before you touch any detail.
beats.on_screen: Side view with the four volumes outlined
beats.label: saucer, hull, nacelles, neck

beats.narration_text: Checkpoint two: the saucer. It's a lens shape with a red edge and a glass dome on top. Draw half its profile and spin it with the Screw modifier, or the Spin tool. That's a lathe. Here's a real warning from this model: Grok Bot's saucer came out too thin, so check its thickness in the side view.
beats.on_screen: Side view crop on the saucer, then bridge close-up
beats.label: saucer thickness, dome

beats.narration_text: Checkpoint three: the secondary hull and nacelles, also lathed from profiles. Again from the review: the secondary hull here is too small. Size it against the saucer in the side view before you move on.
beats.label: secondary hull size

beats.narration_text: Checkpoint four: the neck and pylons that connect everything. Use rounded beams, made with a Bevel modifier, and put each part's origin where it attaches. In this model the neck is barely visible, so make yours thick enough to read in the side view.
beats.on_screen: Hero and rear three-quarter, neck and pylons highlighted
beats.label: neck, pylons

beats.narration_text: Checkpoint five: one porthole first. A cream ring placed on the saucer surface. Get it seated, then repeat it around the ring with radial duplication, at the spacing in the top view.
beats.on_screen: Top view crop on the porthole ring
beats.label: porthole spacing

beats.narration_text: The nacelle details: red caps, cream rings and a red stripe panel that follows the curve. And the deflector, a set of nested cream rings. Build one ring, then the next. The bumper lights in this model read as tiles, so give yours rounder shapes.
beats.label: caps, rings, stripes, deflector

beats.narration_text: Checkpoint six: materials once the shape holds. Blue-grey plastic, cream trim, red accents, clear glass for the dome. Use neutral lights, and compare colours with the concept.
beats.label: palette

beats.narration_text: Checkpoint seven: compare against the same views every round. Your correction prompt fixes the biggest mismatch only: thicken the saucer, grow the secondary hull, keep the nacelles where they are, and re-render without moving the cameras.
beats.on_screen: Top and front vs blueprint comparisons
beats.label: mismatch

beats.narration_text: This one took nine rounds. Professor Bear said, about the concept, I love it. It's fun. You definitely recognize the Enterprise, but it's not the Enterprise. Grok Bot scores round 9 about six out of ten. His verdict on the model is still pending.
beats.label: r1 to r9

beats.narration_text: Checkpoint eight: save numbered files and export a glTF. Re-open it and check the size and colours.
beats.label: save, export

beats.narration_text: Recap. Four simple volumes first. Lathe the round parts from profiles. Connect them with beams. One porthole before many. Colour last, and compare the same views every round.
beats.on_screen: Recap card over the side view

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Thicken the saucer. Then check two things. Does the side view match the blueprint better, and does the hero view still feel like the toy?
beats.on_screen: Your Turn card with the side comparison

beats.narration_text: Built by Grok Bot. Narration: the Liam voice.
beats.on_screen: Credit card: 'Built by Grok Bot' / 'Narration: the Liam voice'

beats.narration_text: Build a Futurama-Style Toy Enterprise in Blender, from Images. At Nik Bear Brown.
